item.title: Machine learning prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma informed by 3D-genome selected circRNAs
item.description:
Shanshan Yin, Wenqian Yan, Chongchen Pang, Liangjie Liu, Mofan Feng, Zhangli Yuan, Haoyan Chen, Xuanwen Bao, et al.
Big Data Mining and Analytics
DOI: 10.26599/bdma.2025.9020125
Abstract Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) remains a major contributor to cancer mortality, with poor prognosis driven by limited options for early detection and intervention. Circular RNAs (circRNAs), a class of non-coding RNAs with tissue-specific expression and regulatory functions, have emerged as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In this work, we investigate the predictive value of circRNAs in HCC using public datasets GSE155949 (49 HCC + 49 normal samples) and GSE121714 (20 HCC + 10 normal samples), and a suite of machine learning approaches, including logistic regression, support vector machines, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and deep neural networks. To capture circRNA contributions from multiple perspectives, we construct six distinct feature panels, one of which incorporates their spatial distribution within the Three-Dimensional (3D) genome. Our results show that circRNAs selected according to 3D genome loci improves prediction accuracy and enhances generalization by mitigating feature collinearity in small-sample settings. These findings highlight the advantages of integrating 3D genome information into circRNA-based predictive modeling and offer a scalable framework for biomarker discovery and precision medicine in HCC.

item.title: Label distribution learning by mining deep semantic label-specific-features
item.description:
Jing Wang, Jinyao Liu, Lingqi Liu
Big Data Mining and Analytics
DOI: 10.26599/bdma.2025.9020114
Abstract Label Distribution Learning (LDL) is a novel machine learning paradigm that effectively addresses label ambiguity in big data analytics. Despite its success, LDL faces two persistent challenges: feature redundancy in high-dimensional spaces and computational inefficiency with large-scale label sets. Although existing methods alleviate these issues by exploiting label correlations, they generally work in the raw feature space, ignoring the critical role of discriminative Label-Specific-Features (LSF). To address this limitation, we propose a novel LDL approach that considers LSF through mining deep semantics, termed LAMPS. First, the label-semantic encoding module jointly learns label-specific and distribution-level semantics via deep graph autoencoders. Second, the learned deep semantics are fused into an LDL process that considers LSF and distribution-level information. We conduct extensive experiments on 12 real-world datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that LAMPS achieves statistically superior improvements over state-of-the-art LDL baselines in 89.4% of the cases and attains 3.2× speedup on the largest dataset, demonstrating its advantages for processing large-scale LDL data.
